short: The blacksmith's son who planned the Mongol campaigns from the Yellow River to the Danube.
full:
Subutai was born around 1175 into the Uriankhai, reindeer-herding forest people of no standing, and joined Genghis Khan's household as a young man. He rose entirely on ability. With Jebe he ran down Shah Muhammad II, then made the great reconnaissance around the Caspian that shattered a Rus' and Cuman army at the Kalka River in 1223 — a three-year ride of some 8,000 kilometres.

He finished the Jin dynasty in 1234 and was the operational mind behind the western campaign of 1236 to 1242, though Batu held nominal command. The invasion of Central Europe was the proof of his method: three columns entering Poland and Hungary on separate axes, hundreds of kilometres apart, converging within days of each other. Legnica and Mohi were fought two days apart by armies that had not been in contact. Recalled by Ögedei's death, Subutai later campaigned again on the Danube under Güyük and retired to the Tuul River, where he died in 1248, having directed more than twenty campaigns.
